findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0355: References to Unauthorized Database Access through Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0357: References to Oversharing of File-Based Content Providers
findings.explanation:
A content provider is exported with no permission: any installed app can query it. If it is public by design, accept it with a reason.
sync/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: provider app.pennyjar.sync.ReceiptsProvider; exported: yes (android:exported is set)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity is exported with no permission and any app can start it with a page URL of its choice; that page then gets the JS bridge that returns the session token. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:32: HelpActivity exported without android:permission.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: Trusts caller-supplied URL.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Exposes the session token to the loaded page.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:30: activity .help.HelpActivity; exported: yes (android:exported is set); deep link schemes: pennyjar

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
Biometric unlock calls BiometricPrompt.authenticate without a CryptoObject and simply proceeds in onAuthenticationSucceeded; no key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired, so the session token is usable without biometrics.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:51: authenticate() without CryptoObject (event-bound).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/BiometricGate.kt:47: Unlock depends only on the callback.

findings.title: MASWE-0042: Latest Platform Version Not Targeted
findings.explanation:
targetSdk is 34. Since 2026-08-31, Google Play accepts new phone and tablet apps and updates only if they target API 36 or higher (rule checked 2026-11-23).
app/build.gradle.kts:14: targetSdk 34

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0272: Identify Dependencies with Known Vulnerabilities in the Android Project
findings.explanation:
com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.5 is in the affected range of 1 OSV advisory: GHSA-4jrv-ppp4-jm57/CVE-2022-25647. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT). 9 of the other dependencies with exact versions match no OSV advisory, but 2 declarations have no version Ward can read (see evidence). Check those, and transitive dependencies, with a Gradle-aware scanner. OSV Maven data downloaded 2026-11-26T21:30:18.923Z (published Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:33:52 GMT).
gradle/libs.versions.toml:11: version 2.8.5
sync/build.gradle.kts:37: implementation (catalog libs.gson) in module sync
app/build.gradle.kts:45: androidx.compose.ui:ui: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)
app/build.gradle.kts:46: androidx.compose.material3:material3: no version (a BOM or constraint may set it)

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
The exported ReceiptsProvider passes the URI's last path segment into a raw SQL string, giving any installed app SQL injection into the receipts database.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptsProvider.kt:40: Untrusted URI segment passed to query builder.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ReceiptQueries.kt:20: Concatenated into rawQuery.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0394: Missing Input Validation in Custom URL Scheme Handlers
findings.explanation:
The pennyjar://help handler takes the 'page' query parameter and loads it in the JS-enabled WebView with no scheme/host allowlist.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:40: URL parameter read from the deep link.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Used unvalidated as the WebView URL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
The help WebView, which carries a token-returning JS bridge and is meant for help pages only, uses a bare WebViewClient with no shouldOverrideUrlLoading, so it navigates to any site.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:27: No URL-loading restriction.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0204: Insecure Random API Usage
findings.explanation:
Share-link tokens, which grant access to a month's expense report, are generated with java.util.Random.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:11: Non-cryptographic PRNG.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/share/ShareLinks.kt:15: Used to build the access token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0232: Broken Symmetric Encryption Modes
findings.explanation:
Private notes are encrypted with AES in ECB mode.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteCipher.kt:9: ECB transformation used for sensitive notes.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
Keystore keys are 256-bit, but the note-encryption key is a 16-byte (AES-128) key, which the test text deems insufficient.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: 16-byte key array (AES-128).

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0212: Use of Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Code
findings.explanation:
The AES key that encrypts users' private expense notes is a hardcoded byte array wrapped in SecretKeySpec, so anyone with the APK can decrypt every note.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:8: Key material is a hardcoded byte array.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/crypto/NoteKeys.kt:13: Hardcoded bytes are used directly as the AES key for note encryption.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0287: Runtime Storage of Unencrypted Data via the SharedPreferences API
findings.explanation:
With 'Remember me' (on by default) CredentialStore saves the user's email and plaintext password in SharedPreferences.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/CredentialStore.kt:12: Password stored unencrypted in SharedPreferences.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:20: Called on every remembered sign-in.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0233: Hardcoded HTTP URLs
findings.explanation:
Receipt thumbnails are downloaded from an http:// URL through the API client (which attaches the Bearer token), and the network security config permits cleartext.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/Endpoints.kt:6: Hardcoded HTTP endpoint.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/ThumbnailCache.kt:25: Used for a real request.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0282: Unsafe Custom Trust Evaluation
findings.explanation:
UploadClient installs a custom X509TrustManager whose checkServerTrusted is empty and getAcceptedIssuers returns an empty array, so receipt image uploads (with the Bearer token) accept any certificate.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:19: Trust manager accepts every server certificate.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:20: Empty accepted issuers.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
UploadClient's HostnameVerifier always returns true.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/UploadClient.kt:28: Hostname verification disabled.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0226: Debuggable Flag Enabled in the AndroidManifest
findings.explanation:
The release build type sets isDebuggable to true.
app/build.gradle.kts:23: isDebuggable = true

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0227: Debugging Enabled for WebViews
findings.explanation:
WebView debugging is enabled unconditionally at application start, with no FLAG_DEBUGGABLE check.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:45: Unconditional WebView debugging.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0334: Native Code Exposed Through WebViews
findings.explanation:
HelpActivity enables JavaScript and exposes a bridge whose sessionToken() returns the user's session token, and the WebView loads any URL supplied by the exported deep link, so any web page can steal the token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:23: JavaScript enabled.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:28: Native bridge registered for all loaded pages.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpBridge.kt:14: Bridge method returns the decrypted session token.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/help/HelpActivity.kt:43: Loads an attacker-controllable URL with no origin allowlist.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0254: Dangerous App Permissions
findings.explanation:
Location is used only for a one-shot foreground city lookup, yet the app declares and requests ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION and FINE location (coarse would do for a city). Ward's analyzer said: Dangerous (runtime) permissions requested. Check that each is needed for a feature, and that a weaker one (coarse instead of fine location, foreground instead of background) would not do.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: Background location declared without a background feature.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/ui/AddExpenseScreen.kt:81: Background location requested after a foreground city tag.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: Fine location for a city-level tag.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:6: android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:7: android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:8: android.permission.ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
The Mixpanel SDK receives the user's email as identity and merchant names with each expense, and these calls never check the user's analytics consent.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:14: Email sent to Mixpanel as the user identifier.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:22: Merchant names sent with expense events.

findings.title: MASWE-0072: Inadequate Privacy Policy
findings.explanation:
A privacy policy link or text is in the app. Ward doesn't read the policy: check that it matches what the app collects and the Data safety answers.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:44: privacy policy
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:103: privacy policy
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:105: privacy policy

findings.title: MASWE-0076: Lack of Proper Data Management Controls
findings.explanation:
Users can create an account here, but Ward found no way to delete it: no delete-account code, text or link in the scanned files. Google Play requires apps that allow account creation to offer an in-app path to delete the account and its data; a link to a web page counts (rule checked 2026-11-23, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111).
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/AuthRepository.kt:25: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:85: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:96: account creation
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/auth/LoginScreen.kt:99: account creation
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:35: account creation

findings.title: MASWE-0078: Inadequate or Ambiguous User Consent Mechanisms
findings.explanation:
The consent screen stores a choice, but Analytics never reads it: events (including app_opened before consent is asked) are sent whether the user allows or declines.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/PennyJarApp.kt:53: Tracking starts at launch with no consent check.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/analytics/Analytics.kt:14: Identity sent regardless of consent.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0200: Files Written to External Storage
findings.explanation:
Static evidence: the daily backup worker writes the user's full expense history unencrypted to public external storage.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: Unencrypted expense CSV written to shared Documents/PennyJar.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared and AutoBackupWorker writes every receipt (date, amount, merchant, place) as plain CSV to the shared public Documents folder without encryption.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9: Permission to write shared external storage is declared.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:21: Backup directory is in public shared Documents storage.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/backup/AutoBackupWorker.kt:24: All receipts are written there as unencrypted CSV.

findings.title: MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package
findings.explanation:
A helpdesk API bearer token is hardcoded in the app and sent from the client, so anyone with the APK can call the helpdesk API.
app/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/support/SupportClient.kt:35: Hardcoded helpdesk API token.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:13: android:allowBackup="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
The API OkHttp client logs full request/response bodies and headers, which includes the login/register password and the Bearer session token.
sync/src/main/java/app/pennyjar/sync/ApiClient.kt:25: HttpLoggingInterceptor at BODY level logs credentials and Authorization headers in release.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0262: References to Backup Configurations Not Excluding Sensitive Data
findings.explanation:
Backup is on (android:allowBackup="true") and there are no backup rules (dataExtractionRules, fullBackupContent), so every app file goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:13: android:allowBackup="true"
